support: After making the cusp rational, choose beta in E_i with p(beta)=p(g), and set alpha=g beta^{-1}. Then alpha lies in pi and Int(g)k_i(t)=Int(alpha)k_i(chi(p(g))t). A.30 proves exactly this formula.

support: The raw product assertion fails already for rho=-1 and three punctures: with c3=(c1c2)^{-1}, c1^{-1}c2^{-1}c3^{-1}=c1^{-1}c2^{-1}c1c2 is nontrivial. A.29 proves the retained conjugated-power statement and gives an explicit reversal/Hurwitz construction for -1.

place: The VA quotient by 'ce sous-module' | 'ces sous-modules'
support: The map to the compactified curve's homology kills the sum of all lifted cusp-inertia images. Thus either wording must refer to their total sum. A.30 and A.50 use the exact boundary-to-Jacobian homology quotient.
strength: The total-sum interpretation is forced; singular/plural typography is not mathematically distinguishable.

place: Maximal subgroups in pi and the margin 'every nontrivial subgroup'; Gamma^+ | Gamma
support: A.13 refutes the literal unrestricted subgroup statement using pi itself and characteristic normal subgroups. A.14 proves the procyclic cyclotomic version; A.50–53 give additional bare-normalizer cases and precise remaining restrictions. Since Gamma^+ is open in Gamma, 'open image in Gamma^+' and 'open image in Gamma' are equivalent for a subgroup of Gamma^+.
strength: The subgroup statement is refuted literally; no unprinted procyclic or cyclotomic condition is attributed to the manuscript. The two ambient-group alternatives are mathematically equivalent here.

place: Insertion specifying dominant morphisms for full faithfulness
support: A.26 proves the dominant/open-image theorem through the exact groupoid and boundary maps. A.3 shows that point sources produce the section-class map and retain a separate global surjectivity problem. Thus the inserted dominant restriction is mathematically material.
strength: Confirms the restriction's role by explicit maps; it is not expanded to all morphisms.

place: Single-circle and double-circle local outer automorphism groups; margin asking for S_nu commutation
support: The single circle preserves each cusp label, while the double circle additionally fixes the Tate orientation. A.33 defines its ambient section action using Aut(F)×_{Out(F)}GT_0, so arbitrary elements need not preserve a fixed G_Q domain. A.49 shows that even S3 commutation leaves explicit nongeometric classes at the metabelian quotient; it makes no assertion equating the full arithmetic image and GT_0.
strength: Supports keeping both superscripts and the additional margin condition explicit. No unresolved full-group equality is inferred from the quotient calculation.

place: One chosen root of lambda^2-lambda+1 versus the unordered full root orbit
support: A.33 proves that fixing the section at 1/2 and one root section gives G_Q(sqrt(-3)). A.34 proves that fixing the full unordered orbit of both roots gives G_Q. Both calculations retain the projected arithmetic domains, and complex conjugation separates the readings.
strength: Both precise interpretations are computed; the two stabilizers cannot be substituted for one another.
